name: fairy path

attributes.attribute: followed unbending paths even over water and bogland
wind by which fairies hurled objects around a house
house built in it destroyed or made unfit

sources: Danaher, Kevin. Folktales from the Irish Countryside. Cork: Mercier Press, 1967, 251-252.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fairy path is a folkloric motif. In the Irish countryside builders kept their houses clear of the routes the fairies took. Fairies followed unbending paths, even over lakes, bogland, or the sea. A dwelling raised in their path was destroyed or fell unfit to use. Fairies punished builders by hurling objects around with the fairy blast, or by carrying the offender off. Building toward the west was discouraged where fairies were thought to dwell.

okr.objective: Fairy path is an Irish folkloric motif about avoiding fairy routes.
